spec.description:
UpdateGame advances the game state by one tick. The time tick counter increments; if it reaches dayLength, ticks reset, the day number rises, and isDawn is set true. Flags isDaytime and isDusk are derived from the current tick position within the day cycle.

The player's physics are stepped via resolvePhysics: vertical velocity accumulates GRAVITY per tick (capped at MAX_FALL_SPEED), horizontal movement responds to input keys by adding MOVE_ACCEL up to MAX_WALK_SPEED when grounded or MAX_AIR_SPEED when airborne. A jump is triggered on ground after cooldown expires, setting vy to JUMP_VEL and starting a short cooldown and a hold counter; while the jump key is held and the counter remains, vy is decreased by a small amount. Pressing down while grounded on a platform shifts the player downward through it. On ground with no horizontal input, friction reduces velocity toward zero. Collision against solid tiles resolves penetration and zeros the velocity component; platforms act as solid only when the player is falling onto them from above. World edges clamp the position, and falling off the bottom sets player hp to zero.

A use cooldown decrements each tick. While the mouse button is held and cooldown is zero, the selected hotbar item is used: if it is a pickaxe/axe with tool power meeting the TILE_TOOL_POWER requirement of the targeted tile, it damages the tile (damage based on tool power), breaking it when hp depletes, spawning particles, and granting drops from TILE_DROPS to inventory. If the item has a placeTile property, the corresponding tile is placed at the mouse-targeted grid cell unless blocked or overlapping the player. Potions apply their healAmount (capped). Melee weapons generate a damage zone near the player with range and duration drawn from the item’s definition; ranged weapons launch projectiles toward the mouse.

Each enemy gets resolvePhysics (without player input), then runs AI from ENEMY_DEFS: slimes, when on ground and within a range threshold, start a random-length jump timer, then jump with a random upward and horizontal velocity directed toward the player; walkers accelerate toward the player within range and jump over solid obstacles ahead; flyers home toward a point above the player or drift using a phase-based periodic pattern when far away. The enemy’s physics is then updated with the world.

Combat: if the player’s current attack zone overlaps an enemy, that enemy takes damage from the player’s weapon. When the player collides with an enemy and a cooldown allows, the player takes the enemy’s damage, receives a knockback impulse, and becomes temporarily invincible.

Particle lifetimes decrement; expired ones are removed. If the live enemy count is below a fixed maximum, a random check each tick may spawn a new enemy; its type is chosen by biome and depth, placed at a random x near a world edge with an appropriate y.

The function returns an object containing the updated player, the pruned enemies and particles arrays, the time object, and the world.
